result.title: PestWeave: Linking Semantic Modeling and Evidence-Guided Text Modulation through Visual Prototypes for Fine-Grained Pest Learning
result.summary: Agricultural pests threaten crop yield and quality, making accurate pest recognition essential for targeted management and sustainable agriculture. Their diverse appearances complicate recognition and motivate multimodal approaches incorporating complementary species knowledge from text. However, complex backgrounds can obscure discriminative visual cues, while textual descriptions may contain information unsupported by the current image, limiting effective cross-modal fusion. To address these challenges, we propose PestWeave, a multimodal framework connecting content-adaptive visual organization with text fusion through visual prototypes. Its visual pathway augments a Receptance Weighted Key Value (RWKV) architecture with semantic token grouping and three types of auxiliary tokens, enabling content-adaptive scanning and contextual modeling while preserving spatial structure. Feature-similar tokens are reordered into adjacent scanning positions, while cluster prototype, global, and register tokens provide group-level summaries, global context, and additional interaction capacity, respectively. These prototypes also guide text modulation by assessing visual support for semantic components and regulating their relative contributions and overall fusion strength, reducing interference from unsupported descriptions. Extensive experiments on multiple pest recognition datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of PestWeave and its potential for practical pest management.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PestWeave 多模态害虫识别框架：视觉侧在 RWKV 架构上加入语义 token 分组与聚类原型、全局、register 三类辅助 token，实现内容自适应扫描与分组上下文建模；再用这些原型评估文本各语义成分是否被图像支持，据此调节其贡献与融合强度。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「用视觉原型评估文本成分是否被图像支持并调节融合强度」的做法，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与不可支持描述抑制提供可借用的门控线索，但任务为细粒度农业识别，需核查该支持度评分能否用于 latent 状态。
